A fortnight ago I arrived at the Vet's office, I got out of my car, walked round to the passenger side and picked my cat up off the seat. I held him tightly, eyes watered a little.
"Stay strong", I said to myself.
I walked inside, there were three women standing at the counter chatting. I walked across the shop floor.
"Stay strong", I said to myself.
I got to the counter, they probably smiled at me or said "Hi", I can't remember. I opened my mouth to speak.
I choked, no words came out, I burst into tears. I stood there stroking my cat, crying, trying to speak, only emitting choked stutters.
There was much sympathy and "Awwwws" from the three women, one grabbed a box of tissues and placed it on the counter for me.
After what felt like an age, I calmed down enough to tell them that I needed to have my cat put down.
It took me three attempts to be able to say his and my own name.

Chocky had quite a few health problems, at 18, that was to be expected, however the previous night he'd had more trouble than usual breathing. At times he had stopped completely and I could see the panic in his face, he hadn't even the energy to stand up anymore, I knew it was his time and I'd been preparing myself for it for a long time but it was so painful to let him go.

Every day, when I get home from work I still involuntarily check under the fireplace to see if he is sleeping there.
Whenever I finish what I am doing before bed, my first thought is to go and find him to take him with me. I still see him everywhere, every piece of clothing left somewhere, every time my dog leaves one of her toys somewhere, I still check he's not under foot when I'm preparing food in the kitchen.
I hadn't wanted to bring up these feels, didn't really want to be crying at work today but the question provoked me, sorry for that.

Living off the grid is a big choice. The three biggest concerns with this choice is water, energy and heating. About 17 million house hold have wells wich makes getting water less a big deal but expect to pay between $3000 to $15000 for well and pump. Others people use cisterns to collect rain water to use. The use of a septic system can be used to manage wastewater. This allow waste to be broken down and to be distributed away from your home. Energy you can get rid of it all together or utilize solar or wind energy to power you home. As for heat use the use of solar heating, fireplace or wood stoves, or geo thermal are all good choices depending on your living situation. When making the move to living off grid take gradual steps to be more successful. So can you do it?
Living off the grid: can you do it?
I would like to be able to. It seems like a skill that could come in handy. That being said I am not the smartest person.

Takes either very little cash and a lot of effort and strain, or a ton of cash and no effort or strain. Going half way on it is the best but no matter what you do getting it set up and good to go is the hardest part, after that it manages itself if you perform good maintenence and learn to spot problems.

Spent a lot of time at my uncles out at his farm, learnt to make tree traps and how to survive without electricity or water. He'd cut himself off the grid years before and let his farm turn into a wilderness while digging himself a decent four room bunker 16 feet down. We never went in there though because he just lived in the barn mainly hunting rabbits and growing potatoes.

He'd visit our house every few months on his pedal bike, a good 30 miles away, and he'd watch TV although mainly the news and talk about his plans for the next season. I haven't seen him for a year or so but I'll be visiting soon to show him my new motorbike, be interesting to see how he's fairing. He never bothered with solar power or anything, just rainwater barrels and such, but given how cheap they are these days I might mention them to him.
